A byproduct of Muse mania is a spike in CPU-linked stocks like AMD, ARM, and INTC, as agentic AI infrastructure demands significantly more CPU versus prior GPU-heavy iterations. However, sentiment is cooling on the broader AI/data center boom, highlighted by SB Energy delaying its IPO after investors balked at its $50B+ desired market cap.
market_outlook: Mixed to cautious. While AI equities are rallying on Muse enthusiasm, multiple negative AI headlines hit after Friday's close, and SB Energy's IPO delay — the second AI-linked IPO pulled in a week following Holtec — signals growing market skepticism toward the sector. The key catalyst to watch is whether broader AI sentiment can hold up amid this cooling IPO market, and whether Anthropic can still come public by year-end (now targeting November instead of October).

tts_summary:
Here's your midday update for Monday, September 21st.

The headline story today is a split tape in AI. On the bullish side, Meta's personal AI agent — called Muse — has been on fire since launching earlier this month, and the demand surge is lighting up the entire AI complex. But here's the twist: Muse is an agentic AI product, and agentic AI runs on CPUs, not GPUs. That's a big deal. It means the winners today aren't your typical GPU names — it's the CPU crowd. AMD, ARM, and Intel are all catching serious bids as the market reprices the infrastructure stack for this next wave of AI.

Now for the cold water. Despite the Muse mania, there was a wave of negative AI news that hit after Friday's close — and Monday afternoon brought another gut punch. The New York Times reported that Softbank's SB Energy is delaying its IPO. Investors pushed back hard on SB Energy's desired market cap of fifty billion dollars or more, and sentiment on the data center boom is visibly cooling. This is now the second AI-linked IPO to get pulled in a single week — Holtec was the first. Two delays in one week is not a coincidence. The market is sending a message that it's getting more selective, and more skeptical, on high-valuation AI infrastructure names.

That brings us to Anthropic, which is the big IPO everyone is watching. Reports from Friday say Anthropic has pushed its target from October to November. Whether it can actually get out the door by year-end is now the critical question hanging over the whole sector.

So here's the net read: the Muse narrative is real and it's moving stocks, but the IPO market is flashing yellow on AI sentiment. The divergence between public market enthusiasm for AI equities and the cooling reception for AI IPOs is worth tracking closely. Bulls need the Muse hype to sustain and Anthropic to price successfully. Bears will point to the IPO delays as an early warning that valuations have run ahead of fundamentals.

Watch the CPU chip complex — AMD, ARM, Intel — for clues on whether the agentic AI trade has legs into the close. And keep an eye on any further IPO headlines, because right now that's where sentiment is most vulnerable.
